title: A Drop for the Debt
premise: Wren Ravensworth, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map — is confronted by a stranger named Ilse who claims he once saved her life in Prague, a favor he has no memory of performing. The debt she repays drags him into a conspiracy: a stolen ledger of identities that three governments will kill to bury, and an assassin, Corvane, who wears Wren's own face and history. As Wren's polished lies about his past unravel, he discovers the 'favor' was real — he erased his own memory of it to survive. To expose the truth before the dawn extraction flight, he must smuggle the ledger past British, Czech, and American handlers, outwit Corvane at the airfield, and choose between the found family he built and the identity that was stolen from him. He boards the flight not as the man who left, but as the man the truth made him.
about_author: Lena Pemberton is a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade shuttling between Vienna and Prague before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose passports tell better stories than they do.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine night in London: burning a compromised asset's papers, checking his go-bag, rehearsing his cover story for the Meridian Office. Establishes his discipline, his loneliness, and the lie he tells himself — that he has no past worth remembering. Emotional beat: controlled unease.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse finds him at a riverside café and returns a 'favor' — a key to a Prague locker — insisting he saved her there in 2016. Wren remembers nothing. Her certainty rattles him more than the key does. Emotional beat: vertigo; the first crack in his polished identity.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: Wren flies to Prague against protocol. In the locker: photographs of himself he never took, a ledger fragment listing forged identities — including one bearing his birth name. POV alternates briefly with Ilse watching him from across the station. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into hunger for truth.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to My Name
chapters.summary: First contact with Corvane, who calls Wren by his childhood nickname and knows details no file should hold. A near-fatal encounter in a tram tunnel ends in stalemate. Wren realizes the assassin isn't hunting him — he's reclaiming him. Emotional beat: terror fused with recognition.

chapters.title: Meridian Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Wren reports in; his handler, Vance, orders him home and denies everything about Prague. Wren notices the office scrubbing his travel records in real time. He chooses disobedience. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Wren gathers his off-book circle: Mara the forger, Dez the signals man, old Tomas the fixer emeritus. They owe him favors, not loyalty — yet they come anyway. Planning the ledger retrieval begins. Emotional beat: warmth he doesn't know how to accept.

chapters.title: What Ilse Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV chapter. Her full account of Prague 2016: a bloodied stranger who carried her out of a burning safehouse and begged her to forget him. She never did. Emotional beat: tenderness aimed at a man who can't receive it.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One File
chapters.summary: The ledger's scope revealed: it documents a joint black program trading identities across British, Czech, and American lines. Each government believes only it holds copies. Wren holds the master. Emotional beat: the weight of being the most dangerous man in Europe.

chapters.title: Vance's Offer
chapters.summary: Vance corners Wren in Vienna: surrender the ledger, get a new name, a clean slate — the same deal, Wren realizes, he accepted once before. Flashback fragments surface: a clinic, a needle, a choice. Emotional beat: horror dawning over déjà vu.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: Recovered memory chapter. Wren was the program's architect-turned-whistleblower; he traded his memories of the ledger for Ilse's life and a fresh start. Corvane is his former partner, left behind. Emotional beat: grief for a self he chose to kill.

chapters.title: Corvane's Side
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He isn't the program's enforcer by conviction — he stayed behind so Wren could escape, and has spent years paying for it. His mission: bring Wren back or bury him. Emotional beat: twisted brotherhood, love expressed as threat.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mara's flat under surveillance pressure; the team counts exits, bullets, hours. Dez cracks the ledger's encryption and finds the extraction flight already booked — in Wren's name, by someone inside Meridian. Emotional beat: claustrophobic solidarity.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Tomas is exposed as Vance's informant — but he leaked only enough to keep the team alive, a double game decades old. His sacrifice covers their escape from Vienna. Emotional beat: mourning a mentor whose betrayal was also protection.

chapters.title: Running the Corridor
chapters.summary: A chase across borders by rail and borrowed identities, each checkpoint a coin flip. Ilse proves indispensable, reading rooms Wren misreads. Corvane shadows them, leaving warnings instead of bullets. Emotional beat: momentum, trust hardening under fire.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: In a decommissioned Czech archive, the team verifies the ledger against physical records — and finds proof Wren authored the whole program. Mara falters; Dez stands firm. Wren must decide whether the truth serves justice or just his guilt. Emotional beat: shame met head-on.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Wren contacts all three governments simultaneously, offering the ledger to whichever grants asylum to his team — playing them against each other while Corvane closes in. Vance counter-offers with Ilse's safety. Emotional beat: cold clarity, gambler's calm.

chapters.title: Night Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter at a farmhouse outside Prague: gear checks, confessions, Ilse and Wren finally speaking plainly about what he gave up for her. The flight leaves at first light. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm; love admitted aloud.

chapters.title: Airfield
chapters.summary: The extraction airstrip at 4 a.m. Vance's team, Czech intelligence, and Corvane converge. Wren springs his real plan: broadcast the ledger live, making every shooter complicit in its survival. Chaos erupts. Emotional beat: adrenaline and audacity.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Gun
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren and Corvane face off on the runway; guns drawn, neither fires. Wren offers Corvane the thing he actually wants — absolution and a way out — as the plane engines spool. Vance is arrested by his own allies when the broadcast lands. Emotional beat: mercy as the hardest move.

chapters.title: Boarding
chapters.summary: Corvane takes the bullet meant for Wren — survivable, barely — and stays behind as cover. Wren, Ilse, Mara, and Dez board with seconds to spare as the ledger floods every news desk in Europe. Emotional beat: cost tallied, escape earned.

chapters.title: A Drop for the Debt
chapters.summary: Resolution. Somewhere over the Atlantic at sunrise, Wren reads his true name in the ledger one last time, then burns the page. The debt is paid; the man remains. He unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years. Emotional beat: release, and the fragile start of a self chosen freely.

chapters.title: Epilogue: New Passports
chapters.summary: Six months later. The team scattered but connected — a postcard network, a standing dinner reservation in Lisbon. Ilse arrives unannounced; Wren opens the door before she knocks. Final line echoes chapter one's rule, rewritten: some bags stay packed for leaving; this one stays packed for staying. Emotional beat: found family, kept.
